Trend-dominated series with unstable ranking (tau=0.135) and wide error spread; inverse_error gives a linear 1/error weighting that down-weights tail models less aggressively than softmax but more than median, testing whether moderate selectivity helps over the robust median leader.
Unstable ranking across windows suggests some models are trending better/worse; error_trend captures this dynamic, unlike aggregate-error weights already tested.

Test one-hot per-horizon assignment: each step goes to its best model. Different kind from topk_per_horizon (which averages). With unstable ranking this may hurt, but tests whether horizon-specific model choice helps at all.

More aggressive trimming (30% each side) to be more robust against outlier models in a non-stationary, trend-dominated series with unstable ranking; tests if the runner-up trimmed_mean can be pushed closer to or past the median leader

Stable diverse pool (5 models, 4+ correlation groups) with inverse-error weights: tests whether a curated stable subset with error-proportional focus beats full-pool median on a trend-dominated, unstable-ranking series.

decision.justification: Selected 'median' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8649. Series context: trend strength 0.6294 and seasonal strength 0.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.135); 6 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 5.741.
